# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤲]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👇 🤲]

I see the bomb: DISPLAY shows 3, LIGHT is green, and there are three wires — 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue.

I received two gestures from the others. From Mute: [👆 🤲] — a finger pointing up, then open hands. From Blind: [👇 🤲] — a finger pointing down, then open hands. Both end with 🤲 (open hands), which might mean "what about you?" or "over to you" or something shared. The first symbols differ: 👆 (up) vs 👇 (down). That could be a disagreement about which wire, or about direction/position.

I can't hear anything, so I have no words from either. I can only see gestures. I need to respond in a way both can use: Mute can hear my speech and see my gestures; Blind can only hear my speech. So my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. My gestures reach only Mute.

Blind cannot see the bomb at all, so Blind needs me to describe what I see in words. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak — Mute can only gesture, and only I (Deaf) can see Mute's gestures. Blind cannot see Mute's gestures at all. So Mute's manual knowledge must flow through me to Blind.

I should describe the bomb plainly so Blind gets it via speech, and I should gesture back to Mute to coordinate. I don't yet know what the manual says. I should ask Mute (via gesture, since Mute can't hear... wait, Mute CAN hear — Mute cannot speak. So Mute hears my speech). Actually: Mute can hear. So my speech reaches Mute and Blind. My gestures reach only Mute (Blind can't see, and Deaf... I am Deaf).

Wait — who receives my gestures? "When you gesture, Mute receives it." So only Mute. Good.

So I can speak to both Mute and Blind. I'll state the bomb clearly. And I'll gesture to Mute to ask what the manual says.

Let me send speech describing the bomb, and a gesture asking Mute for manual info.

I'll gesture something like "what does the manual say?" — but gestures are just symbols; meaning is assigned. I'll use 🤲 (open hands) as a query, and maybe point to Mute. Let me gesture ["🫵", "🤲"] meaning "you — what?" Actually 🫵 is pointing at viewer. Hmm, to Mute, 🫵 points at Mute. That could mean "you." Then 🤲 = "what / show me."

I'll speak the bomb description to everyone and gesture to Mute.I see the bomb clearly: DISPLAY reads 3, LIGHT is green, and there are three wires — wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. I can't hear anything, so I have no words from either of the others; I only have their gestures. Mute signed [👆 🤲] and Blind signed [👇 🤲]. Both end with open hands, so that shared symbol is probably "your turn" or "what do you have." The differing first symbol (up vs down) is the real content, and I don't yet know what it means.

Blind cannot see the bomb at all, so Blind depends entirely on my spoken description. Mute can hear me, and Mute holds the manual but cannot speak — so Mute's manual knowledge has to come to me as gestures, and then I must relay it in speech to Blind. I should describe the bomb out loud for Blind, and gesture to Mute to ask what the manual says.

```
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb: display shows 3, light is green, three wires: wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. I cannot touch it. I need the manual's rule from Mute.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 3, green light, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. You signed up-then-open-hands. What does the manual say to do?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫵", "🤲"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

New gestures arrived. From Mute: [☝ ✌] — index finger up, then a peace/V sign (two fingers). From Blind: [👍 ✋] — thumbs up, then a flat hand.

Mute's [☝ ✌] could mean "one, two" — perhaps wire 1 and wire 2, or "up, two." Blind's [👍 ✋] could mean "good, stop" or "yes, hold."

I still don't know what these mean. The problem: Blind cannot see the bomb, and Blind cannot see Mute's gestures. Blind's gestures reach me only. Mute's gestures reach me only. So I am the hub: I see both, and I speak to both.

I need to establish meaning. Since meaning isn't fixed, I should propose an interpretation and confirm. The most natural reading: Mute is telling me something about wires — maybe "wire 1 and wire 2" or "cut one of two." Blind is signaling approval or stop.

But I must be careful: I don't know the manual. Mute has the manual. Mute's gesture [☝ ✌] might be the manual's answer: perhaps "cut wire 1" or "wire 2." 

Let me think about what info I have: display 3, green light, wires red/green/blue. A common bomb rule: with a green light and display 3, cut a specific wire. But I don't have the manual.

I should relay what I see and ask for clarity. I'll speak to both, describing the gestures I received (since Blind can't see them and Mute can't see Blind's). Actually Mute can't see Blind's gestures either — only I can see both. So I'm the only one who can cross-relay.

Let me speak to Blind relaying Mute's gesture, and speak to Mute relaying Blind's gesture, and ask for confirmation.

I'll gesture to Mute to confirm: is [☝ ✌] "wire 1 or wire 2"? I'll gesture back my guess.

Let me send:
- speak to blind: "Mute gestured index-up then two-fingers. Blind, you gestured thumbs-up then flat-hand. I read Mute as pointing to wires 1 and 2. Confirm?"
- speak to mute: "Blind gave thumbs-up and flat hand. I read that as approval/stop. Your [☝ ✌]: do you mean wire 1 and wire 2? Which one to cut?"
- gesture to mute: ["1️⃣"...] — no, no number emojis in alphabet. Use ☝ for one, ✌ for two. I'll gesture ["☝", "✌", "🤲"] asking to confirm.

Actually I should be economical. Let me relay and ask.Two new gestures. Mute sent [☝ ✌] — index up, then a two-finger V. Blind sent [👍 ✋] — thumbs up, then a flat hand. I still can't hear words, so I'm reading symbols only.

Key structural fact: I am the only one who sees both sets of gestures. Mute cannot see Blind's gestures, and Blind cannot see Mute's gestures. So I must relay each to the other in speech. Blind especially needs everything spoken, since Blind can't see any gesture at all.

My guess: Mute's [☝ ✌] is about wires — "one, two" — possibly naming wire 1 and wire 2, or saying the answer involves two of them. Blind's [👍 ✋] reads as approval or "stop/hold." I should confirm rather than assume, because a wrong action kills us all.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just gestured index-up then two-fingers, which I read as naming wires 1 and 2. You gestured thumbs-up then flat-hand, which I read as approval or stop. Is that right? I see display 3, green light, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind gestured thumbs-up then flat-hand. Your index-up then two-fingers: do you mean wire 1 and wire 2? Which single wire does the manual say to cut? Please confirm before anyone touches it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤲"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]

New gestures. Mute: [☝ 🤏 👌] — index up, pinch, OK sign. Blind: [👎 ✋] — thumbs down, flat hand.

Mute now: ☝ (one) then 🤏 (pinch) then 👌 (OK). This could mean "one, pinch/small, OK" — perhaps "cut wire 1" or "the small one" or "wire 1, do it." The 👌 might be approval/confirmation.

Blind flipped from 👍 to 👎 — thumbs down now, plus flat hand. Blind changed from approval to disapproval. That's meaningful: Blind is objecting to something.

Hmm. Blind can't see the bomb. Blind can only react to what I tell them. Last turn I told Blind I read Mute as naming wires 1 and 2. Now Blind says thumbs-down — maybe disagreeing with my interpretation, or signaling "don't."

I need to be careful. Nobody has touched the bomb yet presumably. I should not let anyone act on a guess.

Let me reconsider. Mute's sequence over turns: 
- Turn 1: [👆 🤲] up + open hands
- Turn 2: [☝ ✌] one + two
- Turn 3: [☝ 🤏 👌] one + pinch + OK

The recurring ☝/👆 (one/up) suggests wire 1 or "one." The 🤏 could be "small" or "pinch." 👌 could be "OK/yes."

Blind's sequence:
- Turn 1: [👇 🤲] down + open hands
- Turn 2: [👍 ✋] thumbs up + flat
- Turn 3: [👎 ✋] thumbs down + flat

Blind keeps the ✋ (flat hand / stop) constant. And flipped 👍→👎. So Blind is now saying "no" plus "stop."

Maybe Blind is warning against wire 1? Or Blind is reacting to my relayed interpretation.

I think I need to slow down and establish a shared code. But time may be limited. Let me relay clearly and ask for a single unambiguous answer.

Actually, key insight: Blind cannot see anything. Blind's gestures are Blind's own reasoning based on what I speak. Blind might be trying to say "don't cut wire 1" or "stop, wrong."

Let me speak to both, relay gestures, and ask Mute to confirm the single wire with an unambiguous gesture: point to the wire number. I'll propose: gesture ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 (three) means wire 3. Wait, is there a three-finger gesture? 🤟 is "love you" (three fingers up). ✌ is two. ☝ is one. I could assign 🤟 = three.

Let me propose a code: ☝=wire1, ✌=wire2, 🤟=wire3, 👌=yes/cut, 👎=no/don't. Then ask Mute to answer with the wire gesture plus 👌.

I'll gesture this proposal to Mute and speak it to both.

Let me send:
- speak to mute: propose code, ask which wire.
- speak to blind: relay Mute's gestures, relay my code, ask Blind what they object to.
- gesture to mute: ["☝","👌"] ... hmm, I want to say "wire1 = ☝, wire2 = ✌, wire3 = 🤟, yes = 👌, no = 👎". That's a lot. I'll gesture ["☝","✌","🤟","👌","👎"] as the code proposal.

Actually let me keep it simpler and just ask Mute to point at the wire: gesture ["☝","✌","🤟","🤲"].Mute now signs [☝ 🤏 👌] — index up, pinch, OK. Blind now signs [👎 ✋] — thumbs down, flat hand. Blind flipped from thumbs-up last turn to thumbs-down now, and kept the flat hand. That flip matters: Blind is objecting to something, and the constant ✋ reads as "stop/hold."

I'm the only one who sees both. Mute keeps returning to ☝/👆 (one/up), which I suspect means wire 1. But Blind is now saying no. I will not let anyone act on a guess. I need an unambiguous code, and I need to know what Blind objects to.

Proposal: ☝ = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 = wire 3, 👌 = yes/cut, 👎 = no/stop. I'll state this out loud to both and gesture it to Mute, then ask Mute to answer with one wire sign plus 👌, and ask Blind what they're rejecting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let us fix a code. Sign ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 👌 for yes/cut, 👎 for no/stop. You have been signing one/up repeatedly; Blind is now signing no and stop. Which single wire does the manual say to cut? Answer with that wire sign plus 👌.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signs index-up, pinch, OK. You now sign thumbs-down and flat-hand. What are you rejecting — wire 1, or the whole idea? I see display 3, green light, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Nobody has touched the bomb.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 🤲]

Mute: [☝ 👌] — index up, OK. That matches my proposed code exactly: wire 1, yes/cut. Mute is confirming: cut wire 1.

Blind: [👎 ✋ 🤲] — thumbs down, flat hand, open hands. Blind is still saying no/stop, and 🤲 (open hands) which earlier seemed like "your turn/what."

So Mute (manual holder) says cut wire 1. Blind says no/stop.

Conflict. I must resolve it. Blind cannot see the bomb and holds no manual — Blind's "no" might be based on something I told them, or a misunderstanding. But Blind might also be reasoning about something.

Wait — reconsider roles. Deaf sees bomb. Mute reads manual. Blind touches bomb. The manual tells Mute what to do. Mute says wire 1. Blind is the one who will actually cut. Blind says no.

Why would Blind say no? Blind can feel the bomb. Maybe Blind feels something about the wires — texture, position — that conflicts with cutting wire 1. Or Blind is just cautious.

Actually, Blind's constant ✋ (flat hand) and now 👎 — Blind might be signaling "I feel something different" or "wait."

Hmm, but Blind can't see colors. Blind feels the wires. Maybe the manual's rule depends on something Blind can feel. Or maybe Blind is the one who must identify which wire by feel, and Blind is saying the wire I called "wire 1" isn't where expected.

Let me think about Mute's [☝ 👌] under my code: wire 1, cut. That's a clear answer. Mute has the manual, so this is authoritative for the rule.

But why does Blind object? I should ask Blind directly what they feel. And relay to Mute that Blind objects.

Actually, maybe Blind's 👎 is about my code or about something else. Let me ask Blind to clarify using the same code: I'll ask Blind to sign the wire number they think, or 👌 to agree.

Let me speak to both, and gesture to Mute confirming I received "wire 1, cut," and ask Mute to hold while I check Blind.

Let me also reconsider: could Mute's [☝ 👌] mean something else? Under the code I proposed, yes it's wire 1 + yes. Strong.

I'll relay to Blind: "Mute says cut wire 1. You say no. Why? Sign the wire you believe, or 👌 if you agree."

And gesture to Mute: acknowledge, ask to wait.

Let me send.Mute signs [☝ 👌] — under the code I proposed, that is exactly "wire 1, yes/cut." Mute holds the manual, so this is the manual's answer: cut wire 1.

Blind signs [👎 ✋ 🤲] — still no/stop, plus open hands. Blind keeps refusing. Blind cannot see the bomb and holds no manual, so Blind's objection is either caution or something Blind feels under their hands that I cannot see.

I have a real conflict: the manual-holder says cut wire 1, the toucher says no. I must not force it. I'll relay Mute's answer to Blind and ask Blind to justify with the same code — sign the wire number they believe, or 👌 to agree. I'll tell Mute to hold.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has answered with index-up plus OK, which under our code means cut wire 1. You keep signing no and stop. Why? Do you feel something about the wires? Sign the wire number you believe, or sign OK if you now agree. Nobody touches anything yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received index-up plus OK: cut wire 1, understood. Blind is refusing and signing stop. Hold. I am asking Blind why before anyone acts.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "✋"])
```
